bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM flags off highway patrolling vehicles, directs tech-driven mega plans for Pitri ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM flags off highway patrolling vehicles, directs tech-driven mega plans for Pitri Paksha Mela 2026 ANI | Updated: Sep 26, 2026 17:29 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], September 26 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Saturday flagged off 58 highway patrolling vehicles organised by the Home Department to strengthen highway patrolling, road safety, and police presence on major routes across various districts of Bihar. In addition to this, the Bihar CM visited Rajkiya Madhya Vidyalaya, Ramjichak, Danapur, where he attended the Parent-Teacher Meeting (PTM) and actively interacted with teachers, students, and parents. Meanwhile, looking ahead to the Gaya Ji Pitri Paksha Mela 2026, a unique blend of tradition and technology has been planned under the directives of CM Choudhary to provide special arrangements for pilgrims. To ensure the safety of devotees and prevent children and elderly individuals from getting separated from their families, a system of QR Code-equipped wristbands has been arranged. These wristbands will have the mobile numbers of family members and necessary details recorded on them, ensuring that if someone gets lost, an alert message will reach the family's mobile phone and the pilgrim can be reunited by scanning the QR code. Furthermore, for pilgrims arriving from across the country and abroad, a Google Translator system has been set up at help desks to overcome language barriers, allowing devotees to hear Hindi responses translated into their own native languages. Law and order during the Pitri Paksha Mela will heavily leverage Artificial Intelligence (AI). Officials will receive location-based alerts anywhere crowd sizes increase, and AI, along with advanced cameras, will assist in identifying missing persons by detecting a face in the camera and instantly tracking the person's location. The Gaya city transformation campaign during the mela has seen children playing a crucial role by drawing art related to Lord Vishnu on the walls. Within the Pitru Paksha mela area, arrangements have been made for the free accommodation of 75,348 people daily, alongside 943 toilets, 134 bathrooms, and 74 changing rooms that have been fully prepared. To cater to basic needs, 280 handpumps and 890 taps have been installed for the pilgrims, while drinking water quality is being checked on a daily basis at PHED labs. A total of 70 health camps are operating within the mela area, where 125 doctors and 178 paramedical personnel have been deployed, alongside free primary treatment arrangements provided by the IMA for the pilgrims. For smooth transit, 150 free e-rickshaws are being operated to provide special transport facilities for pilgrims within the area. Additionally, a special arrangement featuring "Jeevika Didi ki Rasoi" has been established to provide high-quality satvik food to pilgrims at a nominal price of just 30 rupees, emphasising the overall commitment to offering superior facilities to devotees during the Pitri Paksha mela. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Prashant Kishor's JSP plans Delhi expansion, to contest MCD, Lok Sabha 2029 and ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor is all set to expand the party’s presence beyond Bihar, with Delhi emerging as its first target. The move comes barely two months after Kishor won the Bankipur Assembly bypoll in Patna. According to the Indian Express report, Kishor will hold a meeting with JSP supporters in Delhi on Sunday, where a steering committee to oversee the party’s activities in the national capital is expected to be announced, according to a report by The Indian Express. Advertisement JSP Eyes Delhi, Focus On Purvanchali Voters Advertisement “The Jan Suraaj Party is now looking to build a presence in Delhi, especially among the city’s sizeable Purvanchali population,” a source said, as per The Indian Express. Several JSP supporters from Delhi who trace their roots to Bihar are expected to attend Sunday’s meeting, which is likely to be held at Lok Kala Manch or Janpath’s Western Court. “The people in Delhi are tired of the BJP and the AAP. Moreover, they have seen Kishor’s vision for Bihar and Bankipur. We are hopeful of doing well in the national capital,” a party insider said. The JSP is also looking for an office in Delhi. Sources said a few locations have been shortlisted, while formalities related to lease and rent are yet to be completed. Steering Committee To Set Up Delhi Unit The proposed steering committee will be the first step towards setting up the JSP’s full-fledged Delhi unit. The committee will be responsible for creating the party’s organisational structure and appointing office-bearers in the national capital, sources said. Those likely to be part of the panel include advocate Tathagath Harshwardhan, son of former Buxar MP K K Tiwari. Harshwardhan had contested the 2025 polls as the JSP candidate from Buxar. Prof Kumar Shantanu of Delhi University’s Deshbandhu College is also expected to be part of the committee. Another likely member is J P Singh, a former Additional Director General of Police of Himachal Pradesh who contested the Chapra seat on a JSP ticket. Other leaders expected to join the committee include Kunwar Chandresh, head of the Bihar unit’s intellectual cell and a former IES officer; advocate Abu Affan Farooquee, chief of the Bihar unit’s minority wing and former AMU Students’ Union president; Priyanka Singh from the party’s Bihar Mahila wing; businessman Ajay Singh; and former ONGC director Badi Ud Doja, a prominent Seemanchal figure and son of former Bihar minister B Doja. JSP Plans To Contest Delhi Polls Speaking to The Indian Express, Kumar Shantanu said the party had already started reaching out to people in Delhi despite not having a formal organisation in the city. “Despite not having a party organisation in place in Delhi, we have been reaching out to people taking Kishor’s message and vision to them. The response has been positive,” Kumar Shantanu said. He said the JSP plans to contest all upcoming elections in Delhi, including the 2027 Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) polls, the 2029 Lok Sabha elections and the 2030 Assembly

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar steps up efforts to expand sugarcane cultivation, revive sugar mills - ChiniMandi
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News AI Representational Image Patna: The Bihar government is stepping up efforts to expand sugarcane cultivation, raise farmers’ incomes and revive the state’s sugar industry, with a farmers’ seminar held in Patna on Friday to promote the crop and familiarise growers with government schemes and new initiatives, Insider Live reported. The seminar, organised as part of the government’s efforts to strengthen outreach to farmers, was inaugurated by Sugarcane Industry Minister Sanjay Kumar. Farmers were briefed on scientific sugarcane cultivation, quality planting material, mechanisation, jaggery production and various departmental schemes. Kumar said the government was working to increase farm incomes and reduce migration from Bihar by improving farmers’ access to quality seeds, modern technology and agricultural equipment. A department-level campaign is also underway to encourage farmers who had reduced or stopped sugarcane cultivation in previous years to return to the crop. The government plans to work with scientists and specialised institutions to provide farmers with technologies aimed at increasing production from smaller areas of land, the minister said. A dedicated portal is scheduled to be launched on September 30 to provide information on farmers’ concerns and departmental schemes. Farmers will be able to register their grievances, track applications and access information on available schemes through the portal. Kumar also said the government was working to revive closed sugar mills and establish new ones. The state has set a target of reviving existing closed mills and establishing around 25 sugar mills over the next five years. A new sugar mill is also planned in Begusarai. Around 99.39 acres of land has been made available to the Sugarcane Industry Department for setting up a mill in the Warisaliganj area, while the process of securing land in other districts is underway. The government expects the expansion of the sugar industry to increase sugarcane acreage, provide farmers with assured markets and generate employment opportunities in rural areas.

bihar_raw_news.content: September 26, 2026 ‘India’s social support system marker of self-sufficiency’ Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Abhinav Kumar Jha Prominent journalist, auditor and author S Gurumurthy, Chairman of the Vivekananda International Foundation (VIF), argued that India’s ancient dietary and social traditions hold answers to some of the world’s most pressing challenges, speaking at a panel discussion on “Ancient Indian Wisdom as a Guide for Viksit Bharat” held at the India International Centre here on Friday. The event was organised under “Bharat Ki Soch Mantrana,” a flagship discussion series, in media partnership with The Pioneer. Making his central argument, Gurumurthy said India’s predominantly vegetarian food culture has allowed the country to sustain the world’s largest human population on a comparatively small landmass. “If all Indians shift to the American way of eating, we will need six times the land we have today. But if the whole world shifted to the Indian way of eating, we would need only 40 per cent of the land currently being farmed,” he said, citing data from Our World in Data to argue that vegetarian diets deliver far greater caloric efficiency than meat-based ones. At the same time, meat production generates significantly higher carbon emissions. Gurumurthy credited India’s ancient physicians and scholars, including the authors of texts such as the Charaka Samhita, with arriving at sophisticated nutritional and medical conclusions through systematic observation, centuries before the advent of modern laboratory science. He said this knowledge was transmitted across generations not only through formal institutions, but through oral traditions, proverbs, and structured teacher-student relay systems such as the Gurukul, embedding scientific understanding directly into everyday cultural habits. He also contrasted India’s family-based social support systems with the Western welfare model, citing a National Bureau of Economic Research study warning of a mounting deficit in America’s social security system by the 2030s. Gurumurthy said Indian households, where extended families routinely live and care for one another without Government intervention, represent a form of social security that predates and, in his view, outperforms state-run welfare systems, citing India’s homeownership rate of around 85 per cent as one marker of this self-sufficiency. Turning to more abstract territory, Gurumurthy invoked the Nasadiya Sukta from the Rig Veda and drew parallels between ancient descriptions of primordial sound and creation and modern cosmological research into the acoustic signatures of the early universe, arguing that Vedic recitation traditions had preserved complex knowledge with mathematical precision across three millennia through rigorously structured oral transmission. The panel also featured R K Pachnanda, Director of Bharat Ki Soch, and Anil Rajput, Secretary of the Cuisine India Society, who joined Gurumurthy to discuss how India’s traditional knowledge systems could inform the country’s path toward becoming a developed nation by 2047. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

bihar_raw_news.content: Home Judgement Scroll Down To Discover Supreme Court Supreme Court Sets Aside High Court Directions on Compassionate Appointments and Restores Government Policy of Class IV Posting. High Court's Mandate to Appoint or Promote to Class III Posts Violated Service Discipline and Government's Reservation of Class III Posts for Promotion. In Favour of Prosecution Admin 2026-09-26 15:20:55 16 Share This Article: Font size: Print Case Note & Summary The Supreme Court heard appeals by special leave arising from different orders of the High Court of Patna, where the High Court had interfered with compassionate appointments made by the Government of Bihar. The litigation concerned dependent sons and daughters of deceased government employees who died in harness and were awaiting compassionate appointments. The Government of Bihar had adopted a policy decision to appoint all such candidates to Class IV posts irrespective of their qualifications. The Co-operative Department prepared a long list of persons awaiting compassionate appointments. A committee consisting of the Secretary, Co-operative Department, Additional Secretary and Registrar was constituted to identify vacancies and recommend candidates. At the relevant time, more than 40 Class IV posts were available, and the committee recommended appointment of all candidates as Class IV employees. Twelve Class III posts were available but were kept reserved for promotion of existing Class IV employees. Some candidates who were appointed as Class IV employees approached the High Court in CWJC No. 739/1991 titled Ghidharya Devi & Ors. v. State of Bihar & Ors. The High Court by order dated August 26, 1991 directed the respondents to consider afresh their appointments to Class III posts either by promotion or fresh appointment in accordance with rules. The review petition filed by the State was dismissed after considerable delay, and appointments were directed to be made by April 30, 1992. The State did not appeal against that order, which thus became final. Following that order, similar directions were given in respect of different persons who had filed separate writ petitions. In some cases, to comply with the High Court orders and avoid contempt, the government upgraded Class IV posts to Class III posts and confirmed candidates as Class III employees. The core legal issue before the Supreme Court was whether the High Court was right in giving directions to appoint the compassionate appointment candidates afresh or promote them to Class III posts, contrary to the government's policy. The State argued that there is no vested right to a particular appointment on compassionate grounds; the policy to appoint all candidates to Class IV posts was reasonable and justified; and 12 Class III posts were legitimately reserved for promotion of existing Class IV employees. The State further argued that the High Court directions, if complied with, would convert all Class IV posts into Class III posts, violating the discipline of service. The respondents relied on the High Court orders directing appointment or promotion to Class III posts. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Cabinet Approves New Proposals Including New Universities - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Cabinet Approves New Proposals Including New Universities 26 Sep 2026 3 min read Why in News? The Bihar Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary , approved 24 proposals on 23 September 2026 , including the establishment of Maa Sita Women’s University in Patna and Ramdhari Singh Dinkar University in Begusarai . Key Points: Ramdhari Singh Dinkar University: The Cabinet approved the establishment of Ramdhari Singh Dinkar University in Begusarai . The university is proposed under the Bihar Special University Act, 2026 . Its jurisdiction will cover constituent and affiliated colleges in Begusarai and Khagaria , except institutions under Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University . Maa Sita Women’s University: The Cabinet also approved the establishment of Maa Sita Women’s University in Patna . It will have jurisdiction over constituent and affiliated women’s colleges in Patna , except those affiliated with Patna University . Livestock Farmers: The Cabinet approved the Mukhyamantri Go-Dhan Vikas Rin Yojana for livestock farmers. The scheme provides 100% subsidy on the interest component of eligible bank loans. Dairy Development: Eight dairy projects were approved for the Kosi region . The projects include the establishment of 500 new milk cooperative societies and expansion of dairy infrastructure. An estimated ₹126.07 crore has been approved for these projects. New Sugar Mill: Approval was given for establishing a new sugar mill at Warisaliganj in Nawada district . It is expected to support sugarcane farmers in Nawada, Nalanda, Sheikhpura and Jamui . Police Modernisation: The Cabinet approved ₹24.50 crore for procurement of 50 drones under the centrally sponsored police modernisation scheme. The drones will support activities such as crowd management, riverine operations, anti-Naxal operations and disaster management . Healthcare Digitisation: The Cabinet approved implementation of e-SushrutNX , developed by C-DAC , in 12 medical institutions . The system will digitise hospital processes beginning with patient registration and other treatment-related procedures. Fisheries Development: The Cabinet also approved ₹195.28 crore for transforming the Siwan Wetlands Cluster into an integrated aquaculture and export-oriented value chain under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) . bihar_raw_news.title: New Amrit Bharat Express Links Gujarat, Bihar via 20 Stations - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News New Amrit Bharat Express Links Gujarat, Bihar via 20 Stations Breaking News New Amrit Bharat Express Links Gujarat, Bihar via 20 Stations By Urban Acres September 26, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp A new Amrit Bharat Express will connect Bhuj in Gujarat with Barauni in Bihar, providing a direct rail link across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar over a 2,532-kilometre route. The service will run three days a week in each direction, according to the railway information reported by Aaj Tak Business. The train from Bhuj to Barauni will operate as train number 19427. It will depart from Bhuj at 5.30 pm and reach Barauni at 4.05 am after completing the journey. The service will run from Bhuj on Mondays, Wednesdays and Saturdays. The return service, train number 19428, will depart from Barauni at 11.55 pm and arrive at Bhuj at 1.15 pm. It will operate from Barauni on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays. The route will include more than 20 stations across the four states. The listed stoppages are Samakhiali, Ahmedabad, Ratlam, Kota, Sawai Madhopur, Gangapur City, Bharatpur, Mathura, Hathras, Bareilly, Izzatnagar, Pilibhit, Lakhimpur, Gonda, Gorakhpur, Siwan, Chhapra, Hajipur, Muzaffarpur and Samastipur. The service creates a direct connection between western and eastern parts of the country without requiring passengers travelling between the regions to depend on separate train services. Its route also links major rail centres in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, giving passengers access to intermediate cities along the corridor. The announcement is particularly relevant for passengers who regularly travel between Gujarat and Bihar, as well as for workers and traders moving between the four states. The route includes Ahmedabad, Ratlam, Kota, Mathura, Gorakhpur, Muzaffarpur and other regional centres, extending the reach of a single scheduled service across a wide geographic area. Barauni is an important rail location in Bihar, while Bhuj serves as a key railhead in Gujarat’s Kutch region. By connecting the two endpoints through established rail corridors and multiple state-level centres, the service adds another long-distance travel option between the western and eastern parts of India. The railway has fixed the operating days and timings for both directions. The supplied announcement does not provide a separate inauguration date or details on fares, coach composition, ticket availability or the number of services planned beyond the three weekly departures in each direction. The next operational milestone will be the commencement of the announced Bhuj–Barauni service. national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar has emphasised the need to harness the possibilities offered by AI, anticipate its consequences and mitigate its risks. The Minister made these remarks while co-chairing an event on ‘AI in the Context of International Peace and Security, with an Emphasis on Maritime Security’, alongside Foreign Minister of Greece George Gerapetritis. During the event, Dr Jaishankar reaffirmed that AI and maritime security remain important priorities for India at the United Nations. He highlighted that the New Delhi Declaration emphasises democratic access to AI resources, building secure and trustworthy systems, investing in human capabilities and harnessing AI for economic growth and social good. He also highlighted that, in the maritime domain, AI can enhance maritime domain awareness, search and rescue, disaster response, identification of suspicious activity and the resilience of ports and critical infrastructure. The Minister added that it can also enable sophisticated reconnaissance, vulnerability mapping and cyber operations targeting vessels, communication networks and undersea infrastructure. Dr Jaishankar underlined that increasing autonomy in maritime systems raises questions of attribution, accountability and escalation, while also compressing decision-making time. The Minister pointed out that, in the maritime domain, the UN Charter and international law, including the law of the sea, remain essential frameworks governing State conduct. He underlined that greater transparency, confidence-building, capacity development, technical cooperation and the exchange of best practices are essential to ensure that AI is developed and used consistently with these principles.
